rule_summary: Emergency-board order whose only command is a report deadline ends on express revocation (usually EO 12553), not on report/standstill; record report date and standstill end as later_events with a 'functionally spent on <date>' note.
evidence_file_lines: jobs/claim-kit/AGENT_PROTOCOL.md:47 'A report deadline is never an end.' | jobs/claim-kit/assemble.py:554-555 'errors.append(f"clause_{index}_report_deadline_is_not_end")' | jobs/claim-kit/status_overlay.py:678-679 'report_deadline_cannot_establish_status' | jobs/claim-kit/excavate.py:318 'kinds.append("report_deadline")' and :342 note 'A report deadline never yields an end candidate' | jobs/claim-kit/batch.py:202-203 'Determine actual report/transfer/completion fact; a deadline/condition is not proof it happened' | jobs/claim-kit/test_assemble.py:366-370 | jobs/claim-kit/evidence_preflight.py:22,291-299 (REPORT_SUNSET warning cites the ruling as owner_rule)
notes: Enforced half = the negative rule (a report deadline cannot be an end/status basis) in assemble, status_overlay, excavate; surfaced to producers in AGENT_PROTOCOL step 3 and batch tasks. NOT found: any code or producer instruction to record the report date / standstill end as a later_event or to add the 'functionally spent on <date>' note (grep 'functionally spent' over jobs/claim-kit, claim-checker, readiness-tracker, claim_gate.py, claim-drafts = 0 hits). No check that the end is EO 12553 / express revocation. evidence_preflight.py:296-298 says the OPPOSITE scope: 'Express termination on/after a report ... do not apply the deadline ruling as an ending waiver' (consistent with ruling's carve-out of clauses with own fixed date/trigger, but it cites the ruling only as a scope fence). Kind 'report_deadline' is regex-assigned (excavate.py:316-318), so enforcement depends on that tag. AGENT_PROTOCOL.md step 3 predates the ruling; the ruling file itself says it is 'now owner-confirmed' (owner_rulings/2026-10-21-report-deadline.md, Consequences).
superseded_or_conflicting: Not superseded. Consistent with D-20261028-evidence-decides ('separate an exhausted command from surviving consequences'; 'Disclosure keeps a gap visible but never fills it'), which actually generalises the 'functionally spent' idea; no conflict found. The 10-28 ruling adds that a later general rule ends a command only if evidence shows it extinguished it, which matches 'ends on express revocation'.

rule_summary: A clause amended by strike-and-insert or restatement continues, amended, until the parent order ends; the amendment is a later_event recording text before and after; whole-section rewrites carry a substance-changed note; 43 clauses in 26 committed claims need re-check.
evidence_file_lines: No implementation found. Searched jobs/claim-kit/*.py,*.md; jobs/claim-checker/checker.py; jobs/readiness-tracker/tracker.py; research/stage19/code/claim_gate.py; jobs/claim-drafts/*; type-rules. Only adjacent: research/stage19/code/claim_gate.py:83-87 and jobs/claim-checker/checker.py:89 validate that clause.later_events exists as a list with an effective_date (structure only, no before/after text field, no amendment-vs-end rule) | jobs/claim-kit/excavate.py:267 'amended\s+by\s+(?:adding|striking|deleting|inserting|substituting...' only classifies amending text when locating ACT provisions | jobs/claim-drafts/AGENT_GUIDE.md:79-80 tells producers to attach later_events candidates (generic).
notes: No tool or producer instruction carries 'amendment is not an end', before/after text, or the substance-changed note; checker/gate cannot detect a committed claim that treats amendment as termination. The ruling's re-check of 43 clauses/26 orders (files codif-b0, b4, b7, i06, i08, rastell-c01, bowditch-y2-02) is a one-off task, not a tool. Whether the re-check was done is outside this search (not verified here).
superseded_or_conflicting: Not superseded. D-20261028-evidence-decides partly overlaps ('separate an exhausted command from surviving consequences'; 'A later general rule ends a command only if something shows it extinguished that command') and pushes the same direction; no conflict. Note the 10-28 rule also says not to ask the owner method questions, so this ruling stands as a method rule agents apply.

rule_summary: A statute/order that does not name the target does not end it; the naming instrument does. Record the unnamed event as a disclosed earlier candidate end (source pinned where held); 6 committed claims get the disclosure flag.
evidence_file_lines: jobs/claim-kit/excavate.py:556-557 'Parent-as-amended reach is a lead only; target membership and exceptions require confirmation.' | jobs/claim-kit/build.py:409 '# Parent-as-amended is a separately identified indirect LEAD, never a legal inference of target termination.' | jobs/claim-kit/AGENT_PROTOCOL.md:141-147 ('cited by number, no change provision located' and name-match leads are 'leads to read, never events') | jobs/claim-kit/BATCH.md:176-180 source_notes 'retain a savings source or ambiguous earlier candidate without inventing an exact dated event'
notes: Only the 'does not name -> not an end' half is carried, and only for parent-as-amended / cited-by-number / name-match leads (leads never events). NOT found: any field, flag or checker rule for a 'disclosed earlier candidate end' on claims for these cases; source_notes (BATCH.md:176-180) is a generic optional place a producer could record it, but nothing requires or checks it for statutes/orders that merely don't name the target. No code distinguishes 'unnamed instrument' vs other cases; the six committed claims' disclosure flag not located in code.
superseded_or_conflicting: Not superseded. Consistent with D-20261028-evidence-decides ('Disclosure keeps a gap visible but never fills it'; later general rule ends a command only if evidence shows it did). Potential tension: the 10-28 rule requires evidence that a general rule extinguished the command, which is what this ruling already says for unnamed instruments; no conflict.

rule_summary: EO 10449 (emergency board never constituted) is treated like the other emergency-board orders: stays on the books until express revocation; the never-constituted fact is a disclosed note.
evidence_file_lines: No code or producer instruction mentions EO 10449 (grep '10449' over jobs/claim-kit, claim-checker, readiness-tracker, claim_gate.py, claim-drafts, type-rules: no hits outside generated dossiers/_attempts data and jobs/ofr-codification-1989/test_codification.py, a test fixture). The generic report-deadline guards (see D-20261021-report-deadline: jobs/claim-kit/assemble.py:554-555) would apply to it only if its text is tagged kind=report_deadline by excavate.py:318.
notes: No order-specific routing, no 'never constituted' disclosure field. It inherits only whatever the generic report-deadline guard does, so the same gap (no disclosed note requirement, no EO 12553 check) applies. Cannot verify from code whether the EO 10449 claim exists.
superseded_or_conflicting: Not superseded. It depends on D-20261021-report-deadline (it 'follows ruling 1'); no conflict with D-20261028-evidence-decides, though the 10-28 rule's 'happened within interval needs evidence' fits the never-constituted fact being recorded as a note not an end.

rule_summary: An 'until' date is recorded inclusive (runs through end of that day) with the exclusive reading stated in the claim as the alternative; each 'further exempt' extension is its own later_event with date and quote.
evidence_file_lines: No enforcement of the inclusive/exclusive disclosure found: grep over jobs/claim-kit/*.py,*.md, claim-checker, readiness-tracker, claim_gate.py, claim-drafts for 'exclusive reading'/'inclusive' returns only unrelated hits: jobs/claim-kit/excavate.py:333 (regex 'to|through|until|on' to extract an end date, no inclusive flag) | jobs/claim-kit/provision_history.py:158,297,303 'known_sunset_end_exclusive'/'end_exclusive' (internal exclusive-end representation for provision histories, opposite default) | jobs/claim-kit/OCCURRENCE_INTERVALS.md:19 and factual_events.py:26 'inclusive' (occurrence intervals, unrelated). 'Further exempt': jobs/claim-kit/AGENT_PROTOCOL.md:141-147 and excavate.py:585-587 treat 'be further exempted ... by Executive Order No. 6088' as a cited-by-number lead 'never events'; jobs/claim-kit/test_build.py:355,381 test that the text is preserved as ACTOR_TEXT.
notes: Nothing instructs producers or checks that an 'until' end is inclusive with the exclusive alternative disclosed, and nothing models each 'further exempt' extension as its own dated later_event (the claim-kit treatment is the reverse: such citing orders are leads, never events, AGENT_PROTOCOL.md:146). The provision_history exclusive-end field is a different data model and may conflict in convention. Ruling named six orders (EO 8554, 8392, 8828, 8058, 7300, 6933); no order-specific handling found.
superseded_or_conflicting: Not superseded by a later decision, but a possible tension with D-20261028-evidence-decides: 'Record what the evidence establishes ... best supported date or interval' and 'Disclosure ... never fills' - the inclusive/exclusive pair is a disclosure of both readings and fits it. The 10-28 ruling's TR-CS-WAIVER rewrite (research/readiness/type-rules/TR-CS-WAIVER.json) was not checked for until-date wording.
